brief:
Young amputees in Gaza face mounting obstacles to rehabilitation as they await prosthetics and contend with damaged infrastructure, according to Al Jazeera English. The blockade has restricted the availability of medical supplies and rehabilitation services needed by those who have lost limbs in the conflict. Many lack access to adequate healthcare facilities capable of fitting and maintaining prosthetic devices.

Mobility challenges compound their hardship, as widespread destruction has damaged streets and public spaces throughout the territory. Amputees struggle with basic movement and daily activities, often dependent on family members for assistance. Without functioning prosthetics or accessible pathways, returning to employment and independent life remains distant for many, leaving them confined to their homes and facing an uncertain future.
dek: Young amputees in Gaza face harsh realities, awaiting prosthetics and battling mobility hurdles.
title: Gaza amputees struggle to rebuild lives amid blockade
